answer: A collateralized bonding mechanism deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock slashable tokens in escrow before bidding. To prevent an adversary from using a mirror identity across an ocean of addresses, each agent must commit dedicated funds that forfeit upon fraud. The attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of locked capital per identity. However, this entry barrier excludes low-wealth agents and fails against well-financed cartels monitoring an offshore reef.
